subject: Fenced runtime topology Q&A and SOC 2 scoping for GridBank
messages:
From: Paul Burns <paul.burns@gridbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: runtime topology and scoping for SOC 2 questionnaire

Hi Grace / Kimberley —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SOC 2 intake we need a clear diagram and short narrative that shows how Redwood's private (VPC) deployments for Dedicated/Private customers keep inference workloads fenced from shared services. Specifically GridBank needs:

- a concise (single-page) topology that highlights control plane vs data plane boundaries for Private deployments
- the default network controls applied (NSG/security groups, egress restrictions, KMS boundaries)
- any configurable hardening knobs customers can set during onboarding

Can you share a first-pass diagram and a one-page mapping to the SOC 2 criteria (network segmentation + logical access) by EOD Monday?

Also flag any items that will require additional artifacts (flow logs, ACLs, or HIPAA/HSM attestations).

Appreciate it — this is on the critical path for our audit team.

Paul Burns
Head of Security, GridBank
paul.burns@gridbank.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Paul Burns <paul.burns@gridbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: runtime topology and scoping for SOC 2 questionnaire

Paul —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass diagram (runtime-topology-v1.pdf) and a short scoping note (soc2-scoping-notes-GridBank.md). High level summary below, then some clarifying Qs so we scope the mapping correctly.

Summary (short):
- Private deployments run in a customer-managed VPC option or Redwood-managed VPC with strict tenant fencing. Control plane components (orchestration, model catalog, billing) live in a separate management VPC with tightly restricted API endpoints. Data plane inference workers run in isolated subnets that do not have inbound internet access.
- Network controls: security groups + subnet ACLs, mandatory egress NAT gateways that route through organization-approved egress filters, and optional VPC endpoints for telemetry.
- Keys: KMS-backed model encryption in transit and at-rest; optional customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key).

Clarifying Qs so we tailor the SOC 2 mapping:
1) Do you need traffic-level ACL examples (CIDR lists) or only the control objectives mapped to our controls?
2) For logs — is GridBank requesting 12 months of flow/connection logs in raw form, or summary attestation that flow logging is enabled?

If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute walkthrough with Kimberly + Marcus tomorrow; that'll let us produce a tighter mapping to the AIC controls.

Attachment: runtime-topology-v1.pdf (diagram, 312KB)
Attachment: soc2-scoping-notes-GridBank.md (2 pages)

—
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Paul Burns <paul.burns@gridbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: runtime topology and scoping for SOC 2 questionnaire

Paul / Team —

A few technical clarifications to support the SOC 2 mapping. I'm dropping the more detailed segmentation spreadsheet as well (network-segmentation-mapping.xlsx). Important points:

- Tenant fencing: each customer's inference runtime executes in dedicated containers on isolated GPU instances (BYO affinity or reserved pools) that are logically mapped to customer tenant IDs. There is no cross-tenant process-level communication.
- Control plane separation: control plane APIs are authenticated with mTLS; access tokens are scoped per-tenant and expire on short TTLs. Control plane endpoints are reachable only from the management VPC and specific operator subnets.
- Egress controls: we support outbound allowlists and an egress proxy that can be enforced per-deployment. For customers requiring maximum assurance, we can route egress through a customer-managed VPC peering with forced-tunnel VPN.
- Evidence we can provide today: VPC flow logs (30 days by default, longer retention available as add-on), KMS key rotation policies, access audit trails for model deployments, and network ACL configs.

Please call out if you need diagram overlays that explicitly annotate which SOC 2 criteria each control maps to — we can add an overlay column in the spreadsheet.

Attachment: network-segmentation-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet, 84KB)

Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Paul Burns <paul.burns@gridbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: runtime topology and scoping for SOC 2 questionnaire

Thanks Grace / Kimberly — that looks excellent and will work for our auditor intake.

A couple of asks before we close the ticket:
- Can you add a short overlay in the spreadsheet that maps each network control to SOC 2 Common Criteria CC6.0 / CC7.0 (or the auditor shorthand you use)?
- Please confirm whether the default flow log retention can be extended to 12 months and what the delivery mechanism is (S3 export vs on-demand snapshot).

If you can send that by end of week we'll close on our side and include the artifacts in the SOC 2 evidence bundle.

Best —
Paul
Head of Security, GridBank
paul.burns@gridbank.com
